verdicts.question: Which reference-price sources can Luma.Green use legally and cheaply: MCX delayed data (terms and yearly cost through an authorised vendor), a BigMint data licence (price), mill price notices (paper mills publishing waste-paper buying prices)? May anonymised yard buy-price posts be combined into a public board line?
verdicts.problems: Verification limits first: no WebSearch could be run (the session's 200-search budget was already spent before this pass) and page fetches are refused, so none of the 14 cited sources was confirmed by a snippet; checks below use the repository's sibling research clusters and the founder's refined-chain doc. (1) The MCX figures that drive the budget line (Rs 2,00,000/yr for 15-min delayed, 80% for a single segment, Rs 1,00,000 connectivity, the Rs 300/terminal/month vendor entitlement, the 'policy document dated 10 Jul 2026') are not confirmed by any snippet; the only local corroboration is the founder's plan (docs/plan/inputs/.../platform-plan-refined-material-chain.md line 99: 'MCX allows only delayed data on public sites under an agreement'). The arithmetic is fine (2,00,000+1,00,000 = 3,00,000 x 1.18 = 3,54,000; website-only 1,60,000+1,00,000 = 2,60,000 x 1.18 = 3,06,800, so 'Rs 3.1-3.5 lakh' checks out) but the inputs are unverified. (2) BigMint terms, the 'slight premium' redistribution wording and 'no paper series' are not confirmed by snippet. (3) The three Pulp & Paper Times IRPTA figures (Rs 15.80/kg Meerut, Rs 13-13.5/kg southern mills, Rs 20,500/MT) are not confirmed by snippet and the newest is 20 months old; the founder's plan (line 69) records a Sept 2026 event ('mills cut scrap buying by 50-60%') that the answer does not mention, so the mill-side picture is stale. (4) The most serious gap is legal: the answer says 'India has no formal safe harbour' and leans on the EU 2023 Horizontal Guidelines, but omits the Competition (Amendment) Act 2023 proviso to section 3(3) (in force from 18/19 May 2023), which presumes a party 'not engaged in identical or similar trade' to be part of a price arrangement 'if it participates or intends to participate in the furtherance of such agreement' — the hub-and-spoke rule aimed exactly at a platform that collects and republishes competitors' buying prices. The repo's risk-guards cluster documents this (CCI salient-features booklet, 23 May 2023; SCC Online, 5 Oct 2023) together with newer CCI orders the answer also missed: Trustees' Association of India held guilty under s.3(3) for fixing minimum fees (reported 3 Sep 2026) and the Agro Input Dealers Association penalised for coordinating members (order of 21 Aug 2026), plus Samir Agrawal v CCI (SC, 15 Dec 2020) as the favourable precedent. With that proviso, 'yards blind to each other's posts' is necessary but not sufficient: the aggregated line itself is the thing Luma.Green would be 'furthering'. (5) Refined material chain: the answer speaks of 'yard buy-price posts' and 'mill' quotes without mapping them to the founder's five price levels or material states. The aggregated yard line is an L2 (yard -> kabadiwala) price for S1/S2 material; a kraft-mill gate quote is an L3 line (recycler buying S3 baled paper); MCX/BigMint series are L4/L5 references for S7 ingot/billet, not scrap. It also ignores L3 prices from the newly added pre-processor role (PET flake, washed flake, granule) and the industrial by-product listings (bagasse, fly ash, slag), for which no exchange or mill notice exists at all. Every published price needs a level and a state tag.
verdicts.correction: Keep the structure of the original answer but with these changes. MCX and BigMint: treat all quoted fees as unverified until MCX's datafeed desk and BigMint sales give written quotes (no snippet or page confirmed Rs 2,00,000/yr, the Rs 1,00,000 connectivity charge, the 10 Jul 2026 policy date, or BigMint's 'slight premium' wording); what is corroborated locally is only that MCX permits delayed data on a public site under a signed agreement and that neither exchange feed nor BigMint covers paper or Bengaluru scrap, so neither belongs on a public screen in the pilot (the founder's plan already says 'no exchange number on any public screen'). Mill notices: no public Indian mill notice was confirmed; the IRPTA trade-press figures are 2023-Jan 2025 and predate the September 2026 mill buying cut noted in the founder's plan, so the only usable L3 paper line is a dated weekly phone poll of two or three Karnataka/Tamil Nadu kraft mills. Aggregated yard board: Indian law is not silent — the Competition (Amendment) Act 2023 proviso to section 3(3) (in force May 2023) presumes a non-competitor platform to be party to a price arrangement if it participates in furthering it, and CCI's 2026 orders against the Trustees' Association (minimum fees, 3 Sep 2026) and the Agro Input Dealers Association (21 Aug 2026) show associations and their facilitators being sanctioned even where members undercut the floor; the favourable precedent is Samir Agrawal v CCI (SC, 15 Dec 2020: a price set unilaterally by the platform and merely accepted by many independent parties is not a cartel). So the safer design is: (a) Luma.Green's own floor and fallback set by the admin from a documented formula (the plan's 28-day median and 75% floor), never consulted with yards; (b) a public L2 line that is a previous-day median and range across at least five verified yards, with no yard able to see another's posted price, no 'suggested' yard price, and a running check on the share of trades struck exactly at the line; (c) counsel sign-off citing the 2023 proviso before launch. Map every reference line to the founder's five levels and states: L1 household (S0/S1), L2 yard aggregate (S1-S2), L3 mill or pre-processor gate quote (S3 baled paper; S5-S7 flake/granule from the new pre-processor role, polled by phone the same way), L4/L5 exchange or BigMint references (S7 ingot/billet) kept admin-only, and industrial by-products (bagasse, fly ash, slag, husk) priced only from dated buyer quotes per tonne since no exchange or association series exists. Budget the MCX line as an open item ('about Rs 3.5 lakh/yr if the vendor list price is confirmed'), not as a fact. Status should be needs-pilot-or-counsel.

verdicts.question: Aluminium cans: should the household price be per kg or per can, and what does a beverage can weigh (cans per kg)? Above the household level, should prices be shown GST-inclusive or exclusive? Should drop-off pay a published premium over doorstep pickup, and is one city-wide floor enough for a pilot? What evidence is there that WhatsApp groups and calls from the next buyer set daily rates for kabadiwalas and yards?
verdicts.problems: Same verification limit: no snippet could be obtained for any of the 21 sources; checks rest on sibling clusters and the founder's doc. What is corroborated locally: The Kabadiwala Bangalore page was read by the materials cluster on 29 Sep 2026 and the founder's plan (line 101) gives 'Rs 60/kg for aluminium cans', so the per-kg pricing and the Rs 60/kg figure stand; the GST placements (4707 5%, 7001 5%, 3915 18%, 7602 18%, 7204 18%) match the scrap-tax cluster's reading of the Gazette copy of Notification 9/2025-CT(R) (Sl. 317, 406, 116, 331, 263), and the same cluster cites the identical TaxGuru pages for Notifications 06/2024-CT(R) and 25/2024-CT; the scraprates.in 10-20 kg minimum and Kabadiwala Online minimum are also cited by kabadiwala-economics. Errors and gaps: (1) The GST-TDS threshold is misstated as Rs 2,50,000 'per transaction' (and 'per invoice' in whoToAsk); section 51(1) CGST Act applies it where the total value of supply 'under a contract' exceeds Rs 2.5 lakh excluding GST, so invoices under one contract aggregate — the scrap-tax cluster (CBIC section 51 text; TaxTMI 11 Feb 2025) gets this right. The answer also omits the deductor's separate REG-07 registration (GSTN advisory 22 Oct 2024) and the yard's self-invoice within 30 days under rule 47A (from 1 Nov 2024), both needed for the CA brief. (2) Rubber waste 4004 at 5% is not confirmed by snippet or by any sibling cluster. (3) A sibling cluster (eway-gst-ops) states plastic scrap is 5%, contradicting this answer's 18%; the scrap-tax cluster's Gazette reading (3915 in Schedule II at 18% since 1 Oct 2021, no scrap change on 22 Sep 2025) supports this answer, but the conflict should be resolved by opening the Gazette PDF. (4) Can weights (14 g, 14.9 g, 11.3 g, 9.5 g) and Ball India's size range are not confirmed by snippet; the arithmetic holds (14 g = 71/kg, 11.3 g = 88/kg, 9.5 g = 105/kg; at 80 cans/kg and Rs 60/kg a can is Rs 0.75) but the '75-100 cans per kg' range is a derivation for a mix nobody has weighed. (5) Kabadiwala Online's minimum is given as Rs 999 here but as 'around Rs 800-1,000' by the sibling cluster reading the same page; Recycle Baba's Rs 5,000/30 kg, the Rs 499 cancellation fee, scraprates.in's 'Rs 5-7/kg below wholesale' and '5-8% above the Karnataka average', Prime Scrap's rates (dated 23 Jun 2026, three months stale), the Play Store 50K+ figure and Systemiq's 68% are all unconfirmed by snippet. (6) The WhatsApp/callback mechanism is, as the answer admits, undocumented; the founder's plan (line 24) notes kabadiwalas run on 'Basic Android, WhatsApp', which is consistent but not evidence of rate-setting. (7) Refined material chain: the rule '18% metal and plastic, 5% paper and glass' holds only for the waste headings at states S0-S3; once a pre-processor produces S7 output the HSN changes (PET granule 3907, aluminium ingot 7601, recovered pulp 4706, rubber crumb 4004) and the rate may differ, so the price record needs an HSN and rate per material state, not per family. Likewise the metal-scrap reverse charge and 2% TDS attach to Chapter 72-81 scrap headings (L2/L3 trades in S1-S4 metal), not to an S7 ingot sold at L4. The drop-off premium and per-can helper are L1-only rules; industrial by-product listings (bagasse, fly ash, slag) are quoted per tonne at L5 and need a unit field (kg, tonne, piece) that the answer's 'per kg' framing does not provide.
verdicts.correction: Cans: price per kg at L1 (Bengaluru lists quote 'Beverage Cans (Aluminium)' at about Rs 60/kg against about Rs 150/kg for other aluminium, corroborated by the founder's plan and the materials cluster's read of thekabadiwala.com on 29 Sep 2026), with an on-screen '~Rs x per can' helper at a placeholder of 80 cans/kg until the pilot weighs 100 mixed cans in week one; the 9.5-15 g per-can literature figures are plausible but unconfirmed here and the Indian slim-can mix has not been measured, so treat 80/kg as a placeholder, not a fact. GST: above the household level show ex-GST base + rate badge + computed total and store base, rate and tax as separate integers. Rates for scrap headings per Notification 9/2025-CT(R) (17 Sep 2025, effective 22 Sep 2025) as read from the Gazette copy by the scrap-tax cluster: waste paper 4707 5% (Sl. 317), glass cullet 7001 5% (Sl. 406), plastic scrap 3915 18% (Sl. 116; back at 18% since 1 Oct 2021), ferrous 7204, aluminium 7602, copper 7404 and e-waste 8549 all 18%; rubber waste 4004 at 5% is unconfirmed and an open item; the sibling eway-gst-ops cluster's '5% for plastic' conflicts and should be settled by opening the Gazette. Because the founder's chain now tracks material states, store HSN and rate per state, not per family: S0-S3 waste headings above; S7 outputs move to product headings (PET granule 3907, aluminium ingot 7601, pulp 4706, crumb 4004) whose rates must be confirmed separately. Reverse charge: since 10 Oct 2024 a registered buyer of Chapter 72-81 metal scrap from an unregistered seller pays 18% under RCM with no threshold (Notification 06/2024-CT(R), 8 Oct 2024) and must self-invoice within 30 days (rule 47A, from 1 Nov 2024); a registered buyer from a registered seller deducts 2% GST-TDS (Notification 25/2024-CT, 9 Oct 2024) where the value under a contract exceeds Rs 2,50,000 ex-GST — per contract, invoices aggregated, not per transaction or per invoice — after registering as a deductor in REG-07. These attach to scrap headings traded at L2/L3 (S1-S4 metal), not to S7 ingots at L4. Households, being unregistered non-business sellers, see one all-in number. Drop-off versus pickup: publish an L1 drop-off premium (equivalently a pickup deduction) and a minimum pickup lot; Bengaluru directories indicate 10-20 kg pickup minimums (corroborated by the kabadiwala-economics cluster) but the 'Rs 5-7/kg below wholesale' spread and the Delhi apps' Rs 999/Rs 5,000 minimums and Rs 499 cancellation fee are unconfirmed, so set the amount from the pilot's measured Saathi cost per stop. Floor: one Bengaluru floor for the pilot, set unilaterally by the admin as Luma.Green's own offer (see question 1's hub-and-spoke point); the '5-8% above Karnataka average' figure is unconfirmed and zone offsets wait for pilot data. By-products: L5 industrial listings (bagasse, fly ash, slag, husk) need a unit field (tonne) and ex-GST display with their own HSN; the per-kg helper does not apply. WhatsApp and calls: the trade is visibly WhatsApp- and phone-first, but no public study documents the group-and-callback rate-setting mechanism and none of the app-download or survey figures could be confirmed here; confirm shop by shop in the pilot. Status: partly.
